steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Line 9x13 inch pan with parchment paper or foil.
Combine oats, flour, butter, honey, brown sugar, baking soda, and vanilla in a large bowl.
Stir in chocolate chips until well combined.
Lightly press oat mixture into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 18 to 22 minutes.
Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then cut into bars. Cool completely in the pan before removing or serving bars.

raw_recipe.headline: Chewy Granola Bars
raw_recipe.description: These homemade granola bars are easy to make with oats, butter, honey, and chocolate chips; customize with your favorite nuts, seeds, and dried fruit.
raw_recipe.name: Chewy Granola Bars

review.reviewBody: these are great! i made mine healthier by limiting the butter to 1/2 cup and compensated by adding in 1 jar of baby food bananas. i also omitted the chocolate chips and instead used craisins and raisins. halfway through the bake time, i removed the pan from the oven and pressed the mixture firmly into the pan again. this helped to prevent them from crumbling. yummy!

We were going through boxes and boxes of store bought chewy granola bars so I searched for a recipe so we could make our own. This one is great. I feel better about my kids eating something homemade without all the processing of packaged ones! We found them a bit crumbly too. A few changes include whole wheat flour in place of white, have increased the honey & butter a bit, and substituted a cup or two of Rice Crispy's in place of some of the oatmeal to make them a bit lighter and crunchy. We have also cut down on the chips to 1 cup as 2 cups were much too sweet for us. They are a favorite by all!

Excellent! I've made these several times. These suggestions from previous reviewers worked best:
1. Increase butter and honey to 1 cup each.
2. Mix WELL (until sticky).
3. Press HARD into pan.
4. Freeze bars to make less crumbly.
I also substitute 1/4 cup Rice Krispies for some of the oats, for better texture.

This has become my go-to recipe for granola bars and I've made them at least 5x now. My house is never without them. They keep very well individually wrapped in wax paper and then sealed in a big plastic bag in the freezer. So I can just grab and go for a hike or long drive. My husband went on a group hike and shared my bars, and relayed they got good reviews. Like some other reviewers, I press the mixture firmly and evenly both before and after it goes in the oven. I'll also wait until it cools, then put in the fridge a few hours/overnight. I also cut them while still in the pan, that seems to help keep the bars tightly together. But I have actually never used chocolate chips for them, I use a combination of dried fruits and nuts in equal volume. Like instead of 1 c. Chocolate chips, I used a 3rd c. Each of dried cranberries, pumpkin seeds, and candied pineapple. I've found it's made this recipe extremely versatile for everyday.

This recipe is a great inspiration. Change it to suit your tastes and make it your own. I recently bought a box of store brand granola bars and they were horrible! So I thought, "I wonder if I can make granola bars?" I started looking for a recipe and found this one. I did not make them exactly as written because so many reviewers had such great changes. 

Instead of AP flour, I made my own almond flour by toasting almond slivers and grinding them up in my Ninja! I used 1/4 cup butter and 1/4 coconut oil (might try all coconut oil next time); 3 cups of oats and 1 cup of rice krispies. I used a scant 1/3 cup each of honey and brown sugar and only 1 cup chocolate chips. I thought they were sweet enough like this. 

I baked them for 20 minutes and then used a silicone cutting mat to press them down as they came out of the oven a bit puffy. After they cooled completely, they were just the right consistency; firm, yet still chewy, not crumbly, and absolutely delicious! 

I cut the 13 x 9 brick into 24 servings. I will never buy granola bars again. I love that I can pronounce every ingredient in these bars and I have total control as to what goes into them.

UPDATE:
I made these again and pressed them down with the silicone mat before baking and they came out great.

I’ve made these for seventeen years - raised my kids on them! If the condition of my recipe image means anything, they’re well loved! * I modify by reducing flour to 2/3 c total. I use half white flour, half wheat, so that’s 1/3c white flour, 1/3c wheat flour. * I had to use earth balance vegan butter for several years due to a dairy allergy that my son grew out of, and they tasted just as great as with real butter. I never add anything healthy, just chocolate chips. These serve the function of treats in our household, not healthy snack :). Im feeling nostalgic because my oldest son just graduated and he asked me to make some for his drive to college. Figured it was time to review this family staple. Thanks for the recipe!

Recipe is great, my husband and kids love it. I recommend adding about 1/2 cup maybe a little more of corn syrup to make it not fall apart. I found they take longer than 22mins. Closer to 25-30mins depending on the thickness. I also used silicone granola bars trays from amazon which made them perfect.

Made these today and they were fabulous! I added an extra 1/4c of honey, cinnamon, dried fruit, coconut flakes and dark chocolate chips. I made sure to press them in the pan, press them again halfway through baking and again when they came out. This did smear the chocolate chips a bit but, when I cut them with a pizza cutter, they didn't fall apart. I immediately wrapped them in foil and put them in the fridge in a Ziplock bag so they're an easy grab-n-go snack.

It's a keeper.?? 2 & 1/2 c oats plus 1 c Rice Krispies & 1 c All Bran. Omit all but 3 TB butter, melted plus 1/3 c applesauce, unsweetened. Omit sugar, honey and raisins. Instead: 1/3 cup agave syrup plus 1/2 c chopped dates. 1/3 - 1/2 c shredded coconut, sweetened, adds chewiness and sweet. No more than 1/2 - 2/3 c dark choc or semi-sweet chips. 1/3 c chopped walnuts just gets lost in the mix, but they're high in omega threes... Don't forget to press press press before, during and after baking - I drizzled 1/3 c maple syrup over the baked, cooled pan letting it sink in before cutting to reduce the inevitable crumbling. With a banana and glass of liquid calcium these bars serve as an excellent on-the-go breakfast or nutritious midday/evening snack. Thank you! (Used Robin Hood Nutri-blend Tastes Like White flour vs whole wheat or all-purpose.)

These are great. We just made them a second time. The whole family loves them. Changes: 4 cups oatmeal and 1/2 cup Rice Krispies. 1 cup milk chocolate chips, 1/2 cup pecans, 1/2 cup coconut. We pressed them down with a potato masher 1/2 way through baking and right when they are done. They stay together well and are so much better than anything you can buy.

Thank you for the great recipe! I want to be more self efficient and less buying store bought items. So the things I have changed is 4 cups of oats, 1 cup of honey, 3/4 cup of butter, no salt, 1/3 pure maple syrup, 1/3 brown sugar. The key is to make sure you MELT the butter. Mix all wet ingredients and dry ingredients seperately. Then mix altogether then add just 1 cup of chocolate chips and 1 cup of mixed nuts and dried fruit. I used mixed nuts and dried cranberries and raisons. If you add more then that then the ingredients wont stick together. Only bake for 18 mins or until the edge is golden brown. You must press mix FIRMLY into the pan before and after baking and let it cool completly before taking out and cutting. Absoloutly will never buy granola bars again in a store this is SOOOO much better...Thank you again for the super recipe
Turned out great! Added a little bit more honey !

This is a recipe for granola, not bars and certainly not chewy. I thought we'd have some nice meat bars for my brother to take to work. But alas we got granola. Still tastes good.But don't think you're gonna get a bar out of this. See my pictures for reference.

This recipe turned out great! I used quick oats instead of rolled because I use what I have and when I put in my tray I pressed down, especially around the edges to make sure it wouldn't come out too crumbly.
I substituted real maple syrup for the honey and used a little more than half of the chocolate chips called for. They were plenty chocolatey and chewy too.

I’ve made several batches of these, took others reviews and upped the butter and honey to 1 cup each. My favorite is adding graham crumbles, dehydrated mini marshmallows and mini chocolate chips, to make a s’mores bar.
I used date syrup instead of honey, added 2 beaten eggs, used chopped dates instead of chocolate chips. They are sticky, but I like them that way.
My family is obsessed with these. I play a little with the brown sugar honey and butter measurements but otherwise keep it exact.
Tastes good, but what I got is a crumble, not a bar. Needs a lot more binder ingredients.
